title: How a Fridge Keeps Food Fresh

cover.alt: An open refrigerator with fresh food and raw meat sealed separately at the bottom.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: A fridge keeps food fresh by keeping it cold. Cold slows the growth of many bacteria that can make people sick. This lesson explains how a fridge keeps food fresh and safe, and what you can do at home.

items.prompt: Where do you keep milk and eggs at home?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: I keep milk and eggs in the refrigerator.

items.prompt: Can you name one food that goes bad quickly outside a fridge?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: Fish or meat goes bad quickly outside a fridge.

items.prompt: How cold do you think the inside of a refrigerator should be?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: I think it should be very cold, maybe around 4 degrees Celsius.

blocks.title: Part 1: Cold Temperature Slows Bacteria
paragraphs: Some bacteria are tiny germs that can make people sick. Many bacteria grow quickly when food is warm. Food-safety guides call 4°C to 60°C the Danger Zone. A fridge should keep food at 4°C or colder. The cold does not kill all bacteria, but it slows their growth. This helps food stay safe longer.

images.alt: A thermometer shows the food-safety Danger Zone from 4 to 60 degrees Celsius.

items.prompt: How does a cold fridge help keep food safe?
items.answer: The cold slows the growth of many bacteria.

blocks.title: Part 2: The Right Temperature Setting
paragraphs: The FDA says a fridge should be at 4°C (40°F) or colder. A freezer should be at -18°C (0°F) or colder. A fridge dial may not show the real temperature. Put a fridge thermometer inside and check it often. Do not pack the fridge too tightly, because cold air needs room to move.

items.prompt: What temperature should a fridge be?
items.answer: It should be at 4°C (40°F) or colder.

blocks.title: Part 3: How to Store Food Correctly
paragraphs: Raw meat, poultry, seafood, and eggs can carry germs. The CDC says to keep these foods separate from other food. Put raw meat or seafood in a sealed container so its juice cannot leak. Keep other foods in covered containers or sealed bags. Clean spills in the fridge quickly so germs do not spread.

images.alt: A gray-haired woman checks covered foods and raw meat sealed separately in a refrigerator.

items.prompt: How can you stop raw meat juice from touching other food?
items.answer: Keep the raw meat separate in a sealed container.

blocks.title: Part 4: Refrigerate Food Quickly
paragraphs: The CDC says to refrigerate food that can spoil within two hours. If the food is in heat above 32°C (90°F), refrigerate it within one hour. Put a large amount of warm food into several clean, shallow containers. Small amounts cool faster. Then put them in the fridge promptly.

images.alt: A gray-haired woman puts leftovers in a shallow container into the fridge near a clock.

items.prompt: How soon should you refrigerate leftovers?
items.answer: Refrigerate them within two hours, or within one hour in very hot conditions.

items.prompt: You have chicken left after dinner. What will you do to keep it safe?
items.answer: Answers will vary. For example: 'I will put it in a clean, shallow container and refrigerate it within two hours. I will check that my fridge is cold enough.'
